artists.biography:
The Molotovs are a London-based 3-piece band whose style, charisma and incendiary live shows have quickly seen them notch up well over 200 live performances, record label interest and an army of admirers that has led to them being described by none other than Pete Doherty as “Fucking Ace” !
Comprising of siblings Mathew (Vocals/guitar) and Issey Carts (bass/vocals) alongside the energetic drummer Ice, the Molotovs effortlessly mix their setlists up from their own self-penned material with a few well-chosen covers, and play with a passion and drive that more than backs up their claim that “nothing gets left in the dressing room”.

perplexity.description:
Wasted On Youth is the explosive debut album by The Molotovs, the London-based sibling duo of 17-year-old guitarist-songwriter Mathew (Matt) Cartlidge and 19-year-old bassist-vocalist Issey Cartlidge, released on Marshall Records. Emerging from the pandemic era, this 11-track collection channels their youthful rebellion into a raucous fusion of new wave punk, indie, garage rock, and Britpop influences, drawing comparisons to The Jam, Oasis, and Inspiral Carpets. Tracks like opener "Get A Life," a sub-two-minute blast of mod-punk fury railing against online trolls, and the swaggering "More More More" burst with raw energy, tight riffs, and synchronous vocal harmonies that capture their live-wire chemistry.

The album's dynamic range showcases Matt's songwriting prowess, blending frenetic anthems with introspective moments—such as the acoustic "Nothing Keeps Her Away," evoking The Jam's gentler side, and the title track "Wasted On Youth," which builds from wistful reflection on self-doubt and lost opportunities into powerful rhythms and solos. Slower funk-infused "Daydreaming" critiques societal pressures on youth, while closer "Today’s Gonna Be Our Day" serves as an optimistic rallying cry against apathy, urging a new generation to seize power.

Critically hailed as a "youth explosion" and proof of The Molotovs as the "next big thing," the record defies genre constraints with its ambitious scope, short sharp songs, and restless punk spirit, though some note its defensive edge amid bright hooks and 'normie' appeal. Kerrang! praised its "punk brilliance" and Sound Of 2026 buzz, cementing its role in reshaping modern British rock.
